generation.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Edit the FIRST reference image, a native game tile atlas, into a production-candidate hand-painted HD atlas. The SECOND reference is the user's approved painting STYLE ONLY; do not copy its scenery, characters, text, cave, lava or UI. Output exactly FOUR columns by SIX rows of square full-bleed cells, portrait 2:3 overall, ideally 1024x1536. No gaps, borders, labels, margins, text or watermark. Preserve all 24 input cells in EXACT row-major order. Within EACH cell preserve the original dominant color, silhouette, relative screen position, overlap, clipping and where shapes meet that cell's edges. Many cells deliberately contain only a fragment: keep those fragments cropped, and do not replace them with complete isolated objects. Keep the same original top-down game-sprite projection and light direction. The first ten cells show warm red/orange or muted slate-blue pointed and rounded layered crowns, including small brown supports only where already visible; follow their original masses rather than inventing new branches or ornaments. The remaining fourteen show clipped irregular brown raised shapes and small brown lumps against grass; redraw exactly the visible shapes and their existing light/shadow placement, do not reinterpret fragments as new complete props. Only repaint what exists. Match the second image's clean hand-painted finish, broad organic color planes, smooth rounded shading and low fine-grain density. Preserve visible raised volume; do not flatten the brown objects into dirt patches. Replace coarse pixel blocks and stair-step painted contours with smooth detailed painted surfaces. Grass remains olive/lime at the original background positions, without flowers or extra stones. No isometric cubes, new heights, perspective changes, new objects, characters, signs, weapons, buildings or decorative additions. Keep every output cell fully opaque. This is a sprite-source atlas, never a scene or a contact sheet with a frame. Geometry and exact cut placement come from the FIRST image; painting style comes from the SECOND.

scope: Visible source colors/silhouettes only; object identity/material/use remains unknown. Native full opacity, selectors, cycles, map/event/rules/save unchanged. Only accepted cell masters enter private catalog, not the whole atlas.
